title: Promises as object not only in general — but applied to me by sure fiducia
source_text: XXIII. Caeterum hic sedulo monent Theologi Reformati promissiones Evangelicas objectum esse fidei justificantis, non simpliciter, quatenus earum veritas in genere consideratur, exempli causa, morte & passione Christi salutem & peccatorum remissionem partam esse omnibus qui in Christum credunt & resipiscunt; sed etiam quatenus considerantur ut ad hunc & illum sigillatim spectantes, & ab eo per fidem apprehendendae, & ipsi applicandae. Non enim sufficit, inquit Andreas Rivetus, loco modo citato, si quis rei gestae historiam, nempe quod Christus passus est, norit; nec etiam si quis assentiatur & credat, Christum esse passum pro peccatis omnium hominum: Sed insuper requiritur, ut accedat fiducia certa, qua firmissime peccator credat, non solum aliis credentibus, sed sibi quoque privatim remissionem peccatorum propter Christi meritum donatam esse, & propter ejusdem satisfactionem in gratiam se esse receptum, idque sibi fiducialiter applicet.
pass_a_gloss: Moreover here the Reformed Theologians carefully warn that the Evangelical promises are the object of justifying faith, not simply insofar as their truth is considered in general — for example, that by the death and passion of Christ salvation and remission of sins have been procured for all who believe in Christ and repent — but also insofar as they are considered as pertaining to this one and that one individually, and to be apprehended by him through faith, and applied to him. For it does not suffice, says Andreas Rivetus in the place just cited, if someone knows the history of the deed done, namely that Christ suffered; nor even if someone assents and believes that Christ suffered for the sins of all men: But further it is required that there be added a sure trust by which the sinner most firmly believes that not only to other believers, but also to himself privately, remission of sins has been given for Christ's merit, and that for His satisfaction he has been received into grace, and fiducially applies that to himself.
pass_b_english: Reformed warn: Gospel promises are object not only as generally true.
Also as pertaining to this and that person one by one — apprehended and applied by faith.
Rivetus: knowing that Christ suffered is not enough; nor assent that He suffered for all.
Need sure fiducia: remission given to me privately for Christ’s merit; received into grace; applied fiducially to myself.
